Define the work around circulation and drainage.

We assess the damaged surface and the way the area is used before selecting a repair. A few settled pavers, a broken wheel stop and recurring ponding need different scopes. We consider surface build-up, falls, drainage and access, then agree the stages and return-to-use conditions.

01 / Vehicle entry at a commercial loading area

Look below the visible defect

Separate loose surface material from movement in the support layer, and mark whether ponding reaches an entry or loading turn. Compare a small isolated patch with staged work that requires a revised pedestrian route and agreed release of completed bays.

We mark damage against bays, access aisles and delivery routes, and check whether water repeatedly crosses the same low point. The plan should show how people and vehicles pass each work stage, including where sections can reopen before later work.

  • Cracked or settled surfaces

    We check the repair area, adjacent surface, use and accessible build-up. A local surface patch and work involving the underlying support must be distinguished before the scope is agreed.

  • Water returns to the same area

    We review falls, accessible drainage points and the reported conditions. Clearing debris, repairing an outlet and changing the surface or drainage arrangement are different work options.

  • Damaged external fixtures

    We inspect agreed bollards, wheel stops and their fixing areas. The condition of the surrounding surface informs whether securing or replacing the item also needs local surface work.

  • Where water keeps pooling

    We trace where water travels from the upper surface or downpipe, then check inlet condition, local falls, rocking pavers and settlement. We separate surface cleaning and clearing from resetting sound paving, repairing a failed base and reviewing the drainage layout. Quotes account for the affected area, base and vehicle loads, protection and staged access. We hand over repaired locations and note any points to recheck after rain.

02 / Paving joints and grade transitions

Materials follow the use of the area

  • Surface and support

    We identify the existing paving or concrete and the condition beneath the affected area. Material selection considers the repair boundary and the connection to retained surfaces.

  • Curing and reopening

    The agreed material and method determine the conditions for returning vehicles or pedestrians. We do not assign one generic reopening time to every repair.

Warehouses & logistics ↗

Keep deliveries and people in the work plan

Mark damaged bays and low spots on delivery routes separately. Agree alternate routes and reopening checks for each stage.

  1. 01

    Agree the work zone

    We review pedestrian routes, vehicles, loading and equipment access with your manager, then identify the area and any staged closures.

  2. 02

    Prepare and repair

    We carry out the agreed removal, substrate or fixing preparation and repair. Further concealed defects are recorded before additional work is settled.

  3. 03

    Check and reopen

    We inspect the completed area and relevant fixtures or drainage, then confirm the agreed conditions for removing restrictions and returning the area to use.

What changes the repair allowance

  • The work below and around the surface

    Area, depth, substrate preparation, drainage connections, matching materials and waste influence the repair scope. Wider structural or drainage work is separately identified.

  • Keeping the site accessible

    Phasing, vehicle routes, loading requirements, access equipment and material curing affect attendance. These arrangements are part of the quotation rather than an assumed detail.

Release traffic by area.

We record the repair area, agreed surface checks and any restriction or curing condition before a bay or path reopens.

Record what is ready to use

We identify the repaired locations, checks completed and reopening arrangements. Any remaining drainage issue, separate investigation or follow-up work stays on the handover list, so the manager can distinguish completed repairs from the next stage.

  • Location and drainage evidence
  • Temporary traffic route
  • Release conditions by area

Common questions

Common questions

Can a few affected bays be repaired on their own?+

We inspect the defect and surrounding conditions first. Where a local repair is appropriate, the scope identifies the affected bays, access and reopening requirements without assuming the whole car park needs work.

Why does water return after the area is cleaned?+

Check debris, falls, outlets and connected drainage together before specifying cleaning or repairs.

When can vehicles use the repaired surface?+

We confirm this from the specified material, method and site conditions. The work plan states the closure and return-to-use arrangements for that repair, including any staged access.
